## 3. Letter of medical necessity — for your doctor to sign

[Practice letterhead]

[Date]

To: [Appeal address from your denial letter]
Attn: [Appeals department name from the letter, or Medical Director if none stated]

RE: [Patient name]  
DOB: [patient date of birth]  
Member ID: [member ID]  
Claim/Reference #: 00000000  
Date of service: 09/14/2026  
Service denied: MRI lumbar spine without contrast, CPT 72148  
Diagnosis: [ICD-10 code(s) from the order]

I am the treating [specialty] for [patient name] and I am writing to request that the denial of the MRI lumbar spine without contrast be overturned.

The patient reports chronic low back pain [duration]. In late August 2026, [he/she] developed new left lower-extremity weakness and numbness. The patient reports completing eight weeks of physical therapy and taking naproxen from [start date of physical therapy] through [end date], without sufficient relief. [Physical exam findings on date of MRI order, including motor strength testing, sensory exam, and straight-leg raise if documented]. Given the new neurologic symptoms and lack of response to conservative measures, [I / Dr. ___] ordered the MRI on [order date] to evaluate for nerve-root compression and to determine whether surgical intervention was indicated. The MRI was performed on 09/14/2026.

### Criteria met

Policy IMG-204 requires "documentation of at least six weeks of conservative therapy unless red-flag findings are present." The patient completed eight weeks of physical therapy and naproxen before the MRI — more than the required six weeks — as documented in [the physical therapy discharge summary / records from dates through dates] and [prescription records]. Additionally, new lower-extremity weakness and numbness is a red-flag finding indicating possible nerve-root compression or cauda equina involvement, which satisfies the policy's exception for red-flag findings and made timely imaging medically necessary to guide treatment decisions [the clinic note from date documents the neurologic findings].

MRI is the standard of care for evaluating radicular symptoms with neurologic deficit to identify surgically correctable pathology and to exclude emergent causes such as cauda equina syndrome. [Cite: the relevant specialty-society guideline or the insurer's own policy criteria that this patient meets.]

Continued denial delays diagnosis of the underlying cause of the neurologic symptoms. Progressive nerve compression may lead to permanent motor or sensory deficit if surgical intervention is postponed.

I respectfully request that you overturn this denial and authorize payment for the MRI performed on 09/14/2026. [If the denial letter prints a peer-to-peer line: I will call the peer-to-peer line at [number from letter] within [timeframe from letter]. / Otherwise: I am available for peer-to-peer discussion at [best days/times and direct phone number].]

Sincerely,

[Clinician name, credentials]  
[Specialty]  
NPI: [NPI]  
Phone: [practice phone] / Fax: [practice fax]

---

## 4. Note for your doctor's office

- This is a pre-drafted letter of medical necessity for the denied MRI lumbar spine (reference 00000000, service date 09/14/2026) — the plan denied it saying the records did not show six weeks of conservative therapy or red-flag findings.

- The letter is ready to review, edit, and sign — it should take just a few minutes. Please correct anything inaccurate and fill in the specifics in [brackets], keeping only what the chart supports.

- Key items to add: the physical therapy start and end dates (showing at least six weeks before September 14), the exam findings from your note documenting the left-leg weakness and numbness, the ICD-10 code(s) from the MRI order, and the clinic-note date when you documented the neurologic symptoms.

- Please print on letterhead, sign with your credentials and NPI, and fax to the insurer's appeals department at [fax number from the denial letter] — also send me a copy for my records.

- The appeal must be postmarked or faxed by March 31, 2027. Please send by [suggested date two weeks before deadline] so there is time if anything needs correction.

- Thank you for your help with this — the letter and records together should meet the policy criteria and overturn the denial.
data.clock: for employer and marketplace plans, the plan must decide an appeal for care already received within 60 days of receiving it (30 days per level if it has two appeal levels); care already received is never expedited
